translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Ten

sentences.zh: 趙知禮 蔡景歷 劉師知 謝岐

translations.literal: Zhao Zhili; Cai Jingli; Liu Shizhi; Xie Qi
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili; Cai Jingli; Liu Shizhi; Xie Qi

sentences.zh: 趙知禮

translations.literal: Zhao Zhili
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili

sentences.zh: 趙知禮字齊旦，天水隴西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhili, styled Qidan, was a native of Longxi in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili, styled Qidan, came from Longxi in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父孝穆，梁候官令。

translations.literal: His father Xiaomu was magistrate of Houguan under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaomu had been magistrate of Houguan under Liang.

sentences.zh: 知禮涉獵文史，善隸書。

translations.literal: Zhili ranged through literature and history and was skilled at clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili read widely in literature and history and wrote a fine clerical hand.

sentences.zh: 高祖之討元景仲也，或薦之，引為記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended him and he was brought in as record-office aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder marched against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended him and he was made record-office aide.

sentences.zh: 知禮為文贍速，每占授軍書，下筆便就，率皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Zhili's writing was ample and swift; whenever he took dictation for military documents, his brush finished at once and nearly all pleased the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili wrote copiously and fast. Dictated army papers left his brush finished in one pass, and almost all pleased the Founder.

sentences.zh: 由是恆侍左右，深被委任，當時計畫，莫不預〔焉〕。

translations.literal: From this he constantly attended at the ruler's side and was deeply entrusted; of the plans of the time none in which he did not take part therein.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was always at the Founder's side, deeply trusted, and party to every plan of the day.

sentences.zh: [1]知禮亦多所獻替。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 1. Zhili also offered much counsel for correction and replacement.
translations.idiomatic: [1] He also offered much counsel on policy.

sentences.zh: 高祖平侯景，軍至白茅灣，上表於梁元帝及與王僧辯論述軍事，其文並知禮所製。

translations.literal: When the Founder pacified Hou Jing and the army reached Baimao Bay, the memorials to Emperor Yuan of Liang and the missives with Wang Senbian discussing military affairs were all composed by Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder crushed Hou Jing and the army reached Baimao Bay, the memorials to Emperor Yuan of Liang and the letters to Wang Senbian on military affairs were all Zhili's work.

sentences.zh: 知禮沈靜有謀謨，每軍國大事，世祖輒令璽書問之。

translations.literal: Zhili was calm and possessed of stratagem; whenever there were great affairs of state and army, Emperor Wen would send sealed letters to ask him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili was quiet and shrewd. On every grave matter of state or army, Emperor Wen sent sealed letters to ask his view.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，為明威將軍、太子右衛率。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was made General of Manifest Prestige and Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was made General of Manifest Prestige and right commandant of the heir apparent's guard.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛將軍，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Guard General and concurrently Front Army General.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right guard general and also front army general.

sentences.zh: 六年卒，時年四十七。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died, at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 詔贈侍中，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant, posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子允恭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yungong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yungong succeeded him.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 2.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 2.

sentences.zh: 蔡景歷

translations.literal: Cai Jingli
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jingli

sentences.zh: 蔡景歷字茂世，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Cai Jingli, styled Maoshi, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jingli, styled Maoshi, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖點，梁尚書左民侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dian was Master of the Left for the People under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dian had been master of the left for the people under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父大同，輕車岳陽王記室參軍，掌京邑行選。

translations.literal: His father Datong was record-office aide to the Prince of Yueyang, Light Chariots, and managed metropolitan selection.
translations.idiomatic: His father Datong was record-office aide to the Prince of Yueyang of the Light Chariots establishment and ran metropolitan appointments.

sentences.zh: 景歷少俊爽，有孝行。

translations.literal: Jingli in youth was handsome and alert and showed filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli in youth was bright and open, and known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 家貧好學，善尺牘，工草隸。

translations.literal: His family was poor yet he loved learning; he was skilled at letters and excelled at cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor he loved learning, wrote excellent letters, and excelled at cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 解褐諸王府佐，出為海陽令，為政有能名。

translations.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as aide in princely establishments, went out as magistrate of Haiyang, and his governance won a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a princely aide, then became magistrate of Haiyang, where his rule won a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，梁簡文帝為景所幽，景歷與南康嗣王蕭會理謀，欲挾簡文出奔，事泄見執，賊黨王偉保護之，獲免。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Jianwen of Liang was imprisoned by Jing; Jingli with the heir of Nankang, Xiao Huili, plotted to seize the emperor and flee, but the affair leaked and he was seized; the rebel partisan Wang Wei protected him and he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Jianwen was held by Jing. Jingli and the heir of Nankang, Xiao Huili, plotted to carry the emperor off, but the plot was discovered and he was arrested. The rebel Wang Wei shielded him and he survived.

sentences.zh: 因客遊京口。

translations.literal: He then traveled as a guest to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He then wandered as a guest to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，高祖鎮朱方，素聞其名，以書要之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified the Founder garrisoned Zhufang and, having long heard his name, summoned him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing fell the Founder held Zhufang, had long heard of him, and summoned him by letter.

sentences.zh: 景歷對使人答書，筆不停綴，文不重改。

translations.literal: Jingli replied to the envoy's letter; his brush never paused and the text needed no revision.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli answered the envoy's letter without lifting his brush and without a single revision.

sentences.zh: 曰：

translations.literal: He said:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote:

sentences.zh: 蒙降札書，曲垂引逮，伏覽循回，載深欣暢。

translations.literal: I have received your gracious letter, bending low to summon me; reading it over and again, I am deeply glad.
translations.idiomatic: I have received your gracious letter, summoning me with such kindness. Reading it again and again, I am deeply glad.

sentences.zh: 竊以世求名駿，行地能致千里，時愛奇寶，照車遂有徑寸。

translations.literal: I venture to think that the age seeks famous steeds; on good ground they run a thousand li; the time delights in rare treasures; on the carriage mirror there is already an inch-sized gem.
translations.idiomatic: The age seeks famous steeds that can run a thousand li on good ground; the time delights in rare jewels, and already on the carriage mirror there is a gem an inch across.

sentences.zh: 但雲咸斯奏，自輟巴渝，杞梓方雕，豈盼樗櫪。

translations.literal: But now Yun Xian plays, and of themselves the Bayu dances cease; catalpa and paulownia are being carved—how could one look to the stables for fodder?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now Yun Xian plays, and of themselves the Bayu dances cease; catalpa and paulownia are being carved—who would still look to the stables for fodder?

sentences.zh: 仰惟明將軍使君侯節下，英才挺茂，雄姿秀拔，運屬時艱，志匡多難，振衡岳而綏五嶺，滌灨源而澄九派，帶甲十萬，彊弩數千，誓勤王之師，總義夫之力，鯨鯢式剪，役不踰時，氛霧廓清，士無血刃。

translations.literal: Looking up to the Illustrious General, Lord, and Marquis under your command: your talent stands tall, your heroic bearing splendid; the age meets hard fortune and your will sets right many calamities; you shake Mount Heng and pacify the Five Ridges, cleanse the Chan source and clarify the nine streams; armored troops number a hundred thousand, strong crossbows several thousand; you swear the army that will restore the throne and gather the power of righteous men; whale and crocodile are cut down, the campaign does not exceed its season, mist and fog are cleared, and soldiers need no bloody blades.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to you, Illustrious General, Lord, and Marquis: talent in full flower, bearing heroic and bright; fortune is hard and your will sets the realm right; you shake Mount Heng and pacify the Five Ridges, cleanse the Chan headwaters and clear the nine streams; a hundred thousand armored men, thousands of strong crossbows; you swear the army that will restore the throne and gather righteous men; enemies are cut down in a campaign that does not outlast its season, the air clears, and soldiers win without bloody blades.

sentences.zh: 雖漢誅祿、產，舉朝寔賴絳侯，晉討約、峻，中外一資陶牧，比事論功，彼奚足筭。

translations.literal: Though Han executed Lu and Chan and the whole court truly relied on the Marquis of Jiang, and Jin attacked Yue and Jun and within and without alike depended on Tao Kan, comparing affairs and weighing merit, how could those be reckoned?
translations.idiomatic: When Han executed Lu and Chan the whole court truly leaned on the Marquis of Jiang; when Jin struck Su and Jun the court within and without alike leaned on Tao Kan—set beside your deeds, what are those worth reckoning?

sentences.zh: 加以抗威兗服，冠蓋通於北門，整旆徐方，詠歌溢於東道，能使邊亭臥鼓，行旅露宿，巷不拾遺，市無異價，洋洋乎功德政化，曠古未儔，諒非膚淺所能殫述。

translations.literal: Moreover you display might in Yan and the eastern lands; caps and coaches pass the northern gate; you array banners in Xu and song overflows the eastern road; you can make border posts lay aside their drums, travelers sleep in the open, lanes lose nothing left behind, markets show no strange prices—vast indeed are your merit, virtue, government, and transformation, unmatched since antiquity, surely not something shallow men could exhaust in telling.
translations.idiomatic: You show might in Yan and the eastern lands; nobles pass the northern gate; you array banners in Xu and song fills the eastern road; border posts lay aside their drums, travelers sleep in the open, no one picks up what another drops, markets hold no strange prices—your merit, virtue, and rule are vast beyond antiquity, not something a shallow man could tell to the end.

sentences.zh: 是以天下之人，向風慕義，接踵披衿，雜遝而至矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the people of the realm turn to your wind and admire your righteousness; heel to toe they open their robes and come in throngs.
translations.idiomatic: So the people of the realm turn to your wind and admire your righteousness; heel to toe they open their robes and crowd in.

sentences.zh: 或帝室英賢，貴遊令望，齊、楚秀異，荊、吳岐嶷。

translations.literal: Some are noble scions of the imperial house, honored wanderers of fine reputation, splendid talents of Qi and Chu, precocious youths of Jing and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Some are noble scions of the house, honored wanderers of fine name, splendid talents of Qi and Chu, precocious youths of Jing and Wu.

sentences.zh: 武夫則猛氣紛紜，雄心四據，陸拔山岳，水斷虯龍，六鈞之弓，左右馳射，萬人之劍，短兵交接，攻壘若文鴦，焚艦如黃蓋，百戰百勝，貔貅為群。

translations.literal: As warriors they bristle with fierce spirit, ambition seizing the four quarters; on land they uproot mountains, on water they cut dragons; with six-jun bows they shoot left and right; with ten-thousand-man swords they close in hand to hand; storming ramparts like Wen Yang, burning ships like Huang Gai; a hundred battles, a hundred victories; troops like pi-xiu gather in hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Warriors bristle with fierce spirit and ambition fills the four quarters; on land they uproot mountains, on water they cut dragons; six-jun bows shoot left and right; ten-thousand-man swords close hand to hand; they storm ramparts like Wen Yang and burn ships like Huang Gai; a hundred battles, a hundred victories; hosts gather like pi-xiu.

sentences.zh: 文人則通儒博識，英才偉器，雕麗暉煥，摛掞絢藻，子雲不能抗其筆，元瑜無以高其記，尺翰馳而聊城下，清談奮而嬴軍卻。

translations.literal: As men of letters they are broadly learned Confucians, men of outstanding talent and great vessel; their ornamented prose shines and their brushwork weaves brocade; Yang Xiong cannot match their pens, Yu Xin cannot surpass their records; a letter flies and Liaocheng falls; pure talk rises and Ying's army retreats.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars are broadly learned, men of great talent and vessel; their ornamented prose shines and their brushwork weaves brocade; Yang Xiong cannot match their pens, Yu Xin cannot surpass their records; a letter flies and Liaocheng falls; pure talk rises and Ying's army retreats.

sentences.zh: 復有三河辯客，改哀樂於須臾，六奇謀士，斷變反於倏忽。

translations.literal: Again there are debaters of Sanhe who change grief and joy in an instant, and strategists of the Six Wonders who reverse sudden change in a flash.
translations.idiomatic: There are debaters of Sanhe who change grief and joy in an instant, and strategists of the Six Wonders who reverse sudden change in a flash.

sentences.zh: 治民如子賤，踐境有成，折獄如仲由，片辭從理。

translations.literal: They govern the people like Zijian and set foot in a district with success; they judge cases like Zhong You and a single phrase decides right.
translations.idiomatic: They govern like Zijian and wherever they step succeed; they judge like Zhong You and a single phrase decides right.

sentences.zh: 直言如毛遂，能厲主威，銜使若相如，不辱君命。

translations.literal: In straight speech they are like Mao Sui and can stiffen their lord's majesty; as envoys they are like Xiang Ru and do not disgrace their ruler's charge.
translations.idiomatic: In straight speech they are like Mao Sui and stiffen their lord's majesty; as envoys they are like Xiang Ru and do not disgrace their ruler's charge.

sentences.zh: 懷忠抱義，感恩徇己，誠斷黃金，精貫白日，海內雄賢，牢籠斯備。

translations.literal: Cherishing loyalty and embracing righteousness, grateful they give themselves; sincerity cuts through gold, spirit pierces the white sun; heroes within the seas—all are gathered in your net.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and righteous, grateful they give themselves; sincerity cuts gold, spirit pierces the white sun; heroes within the seas—all are gathered in your net.

sentences.zh: 明將軍徹鞍下馬，推案止食，申爵以榮之，築館以安之，輕財重氣，卑躬厚士，盛矣哉！

translations.literal: The Illustrious General leaves saddle and dismounts, pushes aside his desk and stops eating, extends rank to honor them and builds lodges to settle them—light with wealth, heavy with spirit, humble in body and thick toward scholars—how grand! how grand!
translations.idiomatic: You leave saddle and dismount, push aside your desk and stop eating, extend rank to honor them and build lodges to settle them—light with wealth, heavy with spirit, humble in body and generous to scholars—how grand! how grand!

sentences.zh: 盛矣哉！

translations.literal: How grand! how grand!
translations.idiomatic: How grand! how grand!

sentences.zh: 抑又聞之，戰國將相，咸推引賓遊，中代岳牧，並盛延僚友，濟濟多士，所以成將軍之貴。

translations.literal: I have also heard that in the Warring States generals and ministers all promoted guest companions; in middle antiquity governors and shepherds all lavishly extended staff—many officers, many scholars: thus the general's nobility is made.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that in the Warring States generals and ministers all promoted guests; in middle antiquity governors lavishly extended staff—many officers, many scholars: thus a general's nobility is made.

sentences.zh: 但量能校實，稱才任使，員行方止，各盡其宜，受委責成，誰不畢力。

translations.literal: Only measure capacity and test truth, call talent and assign office, round pegs in round holes and square in square, each fulfilling his fit; entrusted with charge and held to completion—who would not give full force?
translations.idiomatic: Only measure capacity and test truth, call talent and assign office, round pegs in round holes and square in square, each in his fit; entrusted with charge and held to completion—who would not give full force?

sentences.zh: 至如走賤，妄庸人耳。

translations.literal: As for a runner of low rank, I am but a vain and mediocre man.
translations.idiomatic: As for me, a runner of low rank, I am but a vain and mediocre man.

sentences.zh: 秋冬讀書，終慚專學，刀筆為吏，竟闕異等。

translations.literal: Reading books autumn and winter, in the end I am ashamed before true scholarship; wielding the brush as clerk, in the end I lack a special grade.
translations.idiomatic: I read books autumn and winter and in the end am ashamed before true scholarship; I wield the brush as clerk and in the end lack a special grade.

sentences.zh: 衡門衰素，無所聞達，薄宦輕資，焉能遠大。

translations.literal: A humble gate, declining and plain, with no path to fame; a petty office and light means—how could I reach far?
translations.idiomatic: My gate is humble and plain, with no path to fame; my office petty and my means light—how could I reach far?

sentences.zh: 自陽九遘屯，天步艱阻，同彼貴仕，溺於巨寇，亟鄰危殆，備踐薄冰。

translations.literal: Since the yang-nine met obstruction and Heaven's step was hard, like those honored officials I drowned in the great bandit, repeatedly neared peril, and fully trod thin ice.
translations.idiomatic: Since the yang-nine met obstruction and Heaven's step was hard, like those honored officials I drowned in the great bandit, repeatedly neared peril, and fully trod thin ice.

sentences.zh: 今王道中興，慇憂啟運，獲存微命，足為幸甚，方歡飲啄，是謂來蘇。

translations.literal: Now the royal way is reviving, anxious care opens fortune; to preserve this slight life is already great fortune; I am just now glad for drink and peck—this is what men call returning to life.
translations.idiomatic: Now the royal way revives and anxious care opens fortune; to preserve this slight life is already great fortune; I am just now glad for drink and peck—this is what men call returning to life.

sentences.zh: 然皇鑾未反，宛、洛蕪曠，四壁固三軍之餘，長夏無半菽之產，遨遊故人，聊為借貸，屬此樂土，洵美忘歸。

translations.literal: Yet the imperial carriage has not returned; Wan and Luo lie waste; on four walls remain only the leavings of three armies; through long summer there is not half a bean's yield; wandering among old friends, I borrow for a time; having reached this happy land, truly beautiful—I forget to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the imperial carriage has not returned; Wan and Luo lie waste; four walls hold only the leavings of three armies; through long summer not half a bean's yield; wandering among old friends I borrow for a time; having reached this happy land, truly beautiful—I forget to return.

sentences.zh: 竊服高義，暫謁門下，明將軍降以顏色，二三士友假其餘論，菅蒯不棄，折簡賜留，欲以雞鶩廁鴛鴻於池沼，將移瓦礫參金碧之聲價。

translations.literal: Privately I admire your high righteousness and for a time visit your gate; the Illustrious General has lowered your countenance; two or three scholar friends lend their surplus talk; you do not discard rush and reeds and send a letter bidding me stay—you would set chickens and ducks in the pool with mandarin ducks and swans, and move rubble to share the price of gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Privately I admire your high righteousness and for a time visit your gate; you have lowered your countenance; two or three scholar friends lend their surplus talk; you do not discard rush and reeds and send a letter bidding me stay—you would set chickens and ducks in the pool with mandarin ducks and swans, and move rubble to share the price of gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 昔折脅遊秦，忽逢盼採，檐簦入趙，便致留連，今雖羇旅，方之非匹，樊林之賁，何用克堪。

translations.literal: Formerly Zengzi with broken ribs wandered in Qin and suddenly met Pan Cai; carrying matting he entered Zhao and at once was detained—today though I am a sojourner, compared with that it is not equal; the burden of Fan Lin—how could I bear it?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zengzi with broken ribs wandered in Qin and suddenly met Pan Cai; carrying matting he entered Zhao and at once was detained—today though I am a sojourner, compared with that it is not equal; the burden of Fan Lin—how could I bear it?

sentences.zh: 但眇眇纖蘿，憑喬松以自聳，蠢蠢輕蚋，託驂尾而遠騖。

translations.literal: Yet tiny convolvulus leans on tall pine to lift itself; foolish gnats trust the triple team's tail to run far.
translations.idiomatic: Yet tiny convolvulus leans on tall pine to lift itself; foolish gnats trust the triple team's tail to run far.

sentences.zh: 竊不自涯，願備下走，且為腹背之毛，脫充鳴吠之數，增榮改觀，為幸已多。

translations.literal: I venture without limit and wish to serve as your footman, to be hair on belly and back, and if released to join the number of barking dogs—added honor and changed view would already be much fortune.
translations.idiomatic: I venture without limit and wish to serve as your footman, to be hair on belly and back, and if released to join the number of barking dogs—added honor and changed view would already be much fortune.

sentences.zh: 海不厭深，山不讓高，敢布心腹，惟將軍覽焉。

translations.literal: The sea does not dislike depth; the mountain does not yield height; I dare lay out my inmost heart—may the General read it.
translations.idiomatic: The sea does not dislike depth; the mountain does not yield height; I dare lay out my inmost heart—may you read it, General.

sentences.zh: 高祖得書，甚加欽賞。

translations.literal: The Founder received the letter and greatly admired it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder received the letter and admired it greatly.

sentences.zh: 仍更賜書報答，即日板征北府中記室參軍，仍領記室。

translations.literal: He again sent a letter in reply and the same day appointed him by provisional commission Record-Office Aide in the Northern Expedition headquarters, still heading the record office.
translations.idiomatic: He sent another letter in reply and the same day appointed him record-office aide in the northern expedition headquarters, still heading the record office.

sentences.zh: 衡陽獻王〔昌〕時為吳興郡，昌年尚少，[3]吳興王之鄉里，父老故人，尊卑有數，高祖恐昌年少，接對乖禮，乃遣景歷輔之。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang [Chang] was then administrator of Wuxing; Chang was still young, Editorial footnote marker 3. Wuxing was the prince's native commandery; elders and old friends observed rank by seniority; the Founder feared Chang was young and might receive them with improper courtesy, and so sent Jingli to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Hengyang Chang was administering Wuxing. [3] He was still young. Wuxing was his home commandery; elders and old friends observed rank by seniority. The Founder feared the prince was young and might receive them with improper courtesy, and sent Jingli to assist him.

sentences.zh: 承聖中，授通直散騎侍郎，還掌府記室。

translations.literal: In the Chengsheng era he was appointed Regular Attendant for Direct Communication and again managed the establishment record office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chengsheng era he was made regular attendant for direct communication and again ran the establishment record office.

sentences.zh: 高祖將討王僧辯，獨與侯安都等數人謀之，景歷弗之知也。

translations.literal: When the Founder was about to campaign against Wang Senbian he plotted alone with Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder was about to strike Wang Senbian he plotted alone with Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 部分既畢，召令草檄，景歷援筆立成，辭義感激，事皆稱旨。

translations.literal: When dispositions were complete he summoned him to draft the proclamation; Jingli took brush and finished at once; the wording was moving and all pleased the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When dispositions were complete he summoned him to draft the proclamation. Jingli took brush and finished at once; the wording was moving and all pleased the Founder.

sentences.zh: 僧辯誅，高祖輔政，除從事中郎，掌記室如故。

translations.literal: When Senbian was executed the Founder assisted the government and appointed Jingli Attendant of the Masters of Writing, still managing the record office as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Senbian was killed the Founder assisted the government and made Jingli attendant of the masters of writing, still managing the record office.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，遷給事黃門侍郎，兼掌相府記室。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently managed the chancellor's record office.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 1 (555) he was made attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate and also ran the chancellor's record office.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，遷祕書監，中書通事舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Secretariat Communicating Affairs Attendant, and managed edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne he was made director of the secretariat, secretariat communicating affairs attendant, and manager of edicts.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，坐妻弟劉淹詐受周寶安餉馬，為御史中丞沈炯所劾，降為中書侍郎，舍人如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding, because his wife's younger brother Liu Yan fraudulently accepted horses presented by Zhou Bao'an, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong and demoted to Secretariat Gentleman, his post as attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 2 (558) his wife's younger brother Liu Yan was found to have fraudulently accepted horses from Zhou Bao'an; Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong impeached him and he was demoted to secretariat gentleman, keeping his post as attendant.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，起為鎮東鄱陽王諮議參軍，兼太舟卿。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Jingli was recalled as Adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Pacifier of the East, and concurrently Grand Master of the Great Boats.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Jingli was recalled as adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Pacifier of the East, and concurrently grand master of the great boats.

sentences.zh: [5]華皎反，以景歷為武勝將軍、吳明徹軍司。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 5. When Hua Jiao rebelled, Jingli was made General Who Overcomes the Enemy and army aide to Wu Mingche.
translations.idiomatic: [5] When Hua Jiao rebelled, Jingli was made General Who Overcomes the Enemy and army aide to Wu Mingche.

sentences.zh: 皎平，明徹於軍中輒戮安成內史楊文通，又受降人馬仗有不分明，景歷又坐不能匡正，被收付治。

translations.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Mingche on his own authority in the army executed Interior Magistrate of Ancheng Yang Wentong, and again accepted horses and weapons from surrendered men with unclear title; Jingli again was charged for failing to correct this and was arrested and handed over for trial.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao fell, Mingche on his own authority executed Interior Magistrate of Ancheng Yang Wentong in camp and accepted horses and weapons from surrendered men with unclear title; Jingli was again charged for failing to correct this and was arrested for trial.

sentences.zh: 久之，獲宥，起為鎮東鄱陽王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: After a long time he was pardoned and recalled as Adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Pacifier of the East.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was pardoned and recalled as adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Pacifier of the East.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，都督吳明徹北伐，所向克捷，與周將梁士彥戰於呂梁，大破之，斬獲萬計，方欲進圖彭城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, as commander Wu Mingche marched north in expedition, wherever he went he won; he fought the Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Luliang, inflicted a great defeat, and beheaded and captured tens of thousands; he was about to advance and take Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 5 (573) Commander Wu Mingche marched north and won wherever he went; he fought the Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Luliang, shattered him, and beheaded and captured tens of thousands; he was about to advance on Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 是時高宗銳意河南，以為指麾可定，景歷諫稱師老將驕，不宜過窮遠略。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan was keen on the lands south of the Yellow River and thought command alone could settle them; Jingli remonstrated, saying the army was weary and the generals proud and that one should not press the distant strategy too far.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was keen on the lands south of the Yellow River and thought command alone could settle them; Jingli remonstrated that the army was weary and the generals proud and that the distant strategy should not be pressed too far.

sentences.zh: 高宗惡其沮眾，大怒，猶以朝廷舊臣，不深罪責，出為宣遠將軍、豫章內史。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan hated his damping the men's spirit, was greatly angered, yet because he was an old minister of the court did not deeply punish him and sent him out as General of Far Illumination and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan hated his damping the men's spirit and was furious, yet because he was an old court minister did not punish him deeply and sent him out as General of Far Illumination and interior magistrate of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 未行，為飛章所劾，以在省之日，贓汙狼藉，帝令有司按問，[7]景歷但承其半。

translations.literal: Before he departed he was impeached by flying memorial; because in his days at the capital his corruption was notorious, the emperor ordered the relevant offices to investigate, Editorial footnote marker 7. and Jingli admitted only half.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave he was impeached by flying memorial; his corruption in the capital was notorious and the emperor ordered investigation. [7] Jingli admitted only half.

sentences.zh: 於是御史中丞宗元饒奏曰：「臣聞士之行己，忠以事上，廉以持身，苟違斯道，刑茲罔赦。

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao memorialized, saying: "Your servant has heard that in a gentleman's conduct loyalty serves his superiors and integrity holds his person; if he violates this way, punishment knows no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao then memorialized: "I have heard that in a gentleman's conduct loyalty serves his superiors and integrity holds his person; if he violates this way, punishment knows no pardon.

sentences.zh: 謹按宣遠將軍、豫章內史新豐縣開國侯景歷，因藉多幸，豫奉興王，皇運權輿，頗參締構。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully accuses General of Far Illumination and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang, Marquis of Xinfeng, Jingli: by many strokes of fortune he was early favored at the founding king's side; when the imperial fortune was lifting he took part in the founding structure.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully accuse General of Far Illumination and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang, Marquis of Xinfeng, Jingli: by many strokes of fortune he was early favored at the founding king's side; when the imperial fortune was lifting he took part in the founding structure.

sentences.zh: 天嘉之世，贓賄狼藉，聖恩錄用，許以更鳴，裂壤崇階，不遠斯復。

translations.literal: In the Tianjia era his bribes were notorious; by imperial grace he was recorded for use and allowed to sound again; fief land and lofty rank were not long in returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjia era his bribes were notorious; by imperial grace he was recorded for use and allowed to sound again; fief land and lofty rank were not long in returning.

sentences.zh: 不能改節自勵，以報曲成，遂乃專擅貪汙，彰於遠近，一則已甚，其可再乎？

translations.literal: He could not change his ways and encourage himself to repay partial formation; he then monopolized greed and corruption, manifest near and far—once was already too much; how could there be a second?
translations.idiomatic: He could not change his ways and encourage himself to repay partial formation; he then monopolized greed and corruption, manifest near and far—once was already too much; how could there be a second?

sentences.zh: 宜寘刑書，以明秋憲。

translations.literal: He should be placed in the penal code to clarify autumn law.
translations.idiomatic: He should be placed in the penal code to clarify autumn law.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，以見事免景歷所居官，下鴻臚削爵土。

translations.literal: Your servants jointly propose that, on the matter before us, Jingli be removed from the office he holds and the Court of Imperial Entertainments be directed to strip his fief land.
translations.idiomatic: We jointly propose that, on the matter before us, Jingli be removed from the office he holds and the Court of Imperial Entertainments be directed to strip his fief.

sentences.zh: 謹奉白簡以聞。

translations.literal: Respectfully presenting the white bamboo to inform."
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully presenting the white bamboo to inform."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 於是徙居會稽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was moved to live in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was moved to live in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及吳明徹敗，帝思景歷前言，即日追還，復以為征南鄱陽王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Wu Mingche was defeated the emperor recalled Jingli's former words and the same day recalled him, again making him Adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Campaign South.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Mingche was defeated the emperor recalled Jingli's former words and the same day recalled him, again making him adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Campaign South.

sentences.zh: 數日，遷員外散騎常侍，兼御史中丞，復本封爵，入守度支尚書。

translations.literal: Within several days he was transferred to Extraordinary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, restored to his original enfeoffment, and entered to hold the post of Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Within several days he was made extraordinary attendant of scattered cavalry and concurrently censor-in-chief, restored to his original enfeoffment, and entered to hold the post of minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 舊式拜官在午後，景歷拜日，適值輿駕幸玄武觀，在位皆侍宴，帝恐景歷不豫，特令早拜，其見重如此。

translations.literal: By old form, receiving office was in the afternoon; on the day Jingli took office it happened that the imperial carriage visited the Black Tortoise Observatory; all in office were attending the feast; the emperor feared Jingli would not be at ease and specially ordered early investiture—such was the regard for him.
translations.idiomatic: By old form, receiving office was in the afternoon; on the day Jingli took office the imperial carriage happened to visit the Black Tortoise Observatory; all in office were at the feast; the emperor feared Jingli would not be at ease and specially ordered early investiture—such was the regard for him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以疾卒官，時年六十。

translations.literal: That year he died in office, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died in office, at sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈太常卿，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies, posthumous title Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of ceremonies with the posthumous name Reverent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改葬，重贈中領軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when he was reburied, he was again posthumously made Central Commander of the Palace Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when he was reburied, he was again posthumously made central commander of the palace army.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年，配享高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming he was granted sacrifice in the Founder's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 1 (587) he was granted sacrifice in the Founder's temple court.

sentences.zh: 二年，輿駕親幸其宅，重贈景歷侍中、中撫將軍，諡曰忠敬，給鼓吹一部，并於墓所立碑。

translations.literal: In the second year the imperial carriage personally visited his residence; Jingli was again posthumously made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Center, posthumous title Loyal-Reverent, given one set of pipes and drums, and a stele was erected at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the imperial carriage personally visited his residence; Jingli was again posthumously made palace attendant and general who pacifies the center, posthumous name Loyal-Reverent, given one set of pipes and drums, and a stele was erected at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 景歷屬文，不尚雕靡，而長於敘事，應機敏速，為當世所稱。

translations.literal: In composition Jingli did not favor ornate excess but excelled at narrative; swift to meet the moment, he was praised by his age.
translations.idiomatic: In composition Jingli did not favor ornate excess but excelled at narrative; swift to meet the moment, he was praised by his age.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 劉師知

translations.literal: Liu Shizhi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shizhi

sentences.zh: 劉師知，沛國相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shizhi was a native of Xiang in Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shizhi came from Xiang in Pei.

sentences.zh: 家世素族。

translations.literal: His family for generations was a plain clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family for generations had been a plain clan.

sentences.zh: 祖奚之，齊晉安王諮議參軍，淮南太守，有能政，齊武帝手詔頻褒賞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xi Zhi was Aide-de-Camp to the Prince of Jin'an of Qi and Administrator of Huainan; he had able administration, and Emperor Wu of Qi repeatedly praised and rewarded him in handwritten edicts.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xi Zhi had been aide to Qi’s prince of Jin’an and administrator of Huainan, a capable magistrate whom Emperor Wu of Qi repeatedly praised in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 父景彥，梁尚書左丞、司農卿。

translations.literal: His father Jingyan was Liang Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingyan had been Liang’s left vice director of the masters of writing and minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 師知好學，有當世才。

translations.literal: Shizhi loved learning and had talent for his age.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi was studious and had real talent for his day.

sentences.zh: 博涉書史，工文筆，善儀體，臺閣故事，多所詳悉。

translations.literal: He ranged widely through books and histories, was skilled at literary composition, good at ritual forms, and knew many details of secretariat precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in history, wrote well, understood ceremony, and knew secretariat precedent in detail.

sentences.zh: 梁世歷王府參軍。

translations.literal: Under Liang he successively served as staff officer in princely households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served in several princes’ households as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 紹泰初，高祖入輔，以師知為中書舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaotai the Founder entered to assist the government and appointed Shizhi Palace Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary, in charge of edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaotai began the Founder took power as regent and made Shizhi a palace secretariat attendant-in-ordinary in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 是時兵亂之後，禮儀多闕，高祖為丞相及加九錫并受禪，其儀注並師知所定焉。

translations.literal: At that time, after the military disorders, ritual observances were largely missing; when the Founder was Chancellor and received the Nine Bestowals and then the abdication, all the ritual protocols were set by Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars ritual was largely lost; Shizhi drew up the protocols for the Founder’s regency, the Nine Bestowals, and the abdication.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，仍為舍人。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate he remained Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne Shizhi kept his post as attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 性疏簡，與物多忤，雖位宦不遷，而委任甚重，其所獻替，皆有弘益。

translations.literal: By nature he was blunt and simple and often at odds with others; though his official rank did not advance, his commission was very weighty, and the proposals he offered all had broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt and often clashed with others; though his rank scarcely rose, his trust was great and his counsel was always useful.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩，六日成服，朝臣共議大行皇帝靈座俠御人所服衣服吉凶之制，博士沈文阿議，宜服吉服。

translations.literal: When the Founder died, on the sixth day they completed mourning dress; the court ministers together discussed whether the attendants at the late emperor’s spirit seat should wear auspicious or inauspicious garments. Academician Shen Wen’a argued that they should wear auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder died, on the sixth day mourning dress was completed. The court debated whether attendants at the late emperor’s spirit seat should wear auspicious or mourning dress. Academician Shen Wen’a argued for auspicious dress.

sentences.zh: 師知議云：「既稱成服，本備喪禮，靈筵服物，皆悉縞素。

translations.literal: Shizhi argued: "Since it is called completing mourning dress, it is fundamentally to prepare the mourning rites; all garments and objects at the spirit couch should be entirely plain white.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi argued: "Completing mourning dress means preparing the full mourning rite. Everything at the spirit couch should be plain white.

sentences.zh: 今雖無大行俠御官事，按梁昭明太子薨，成服俠侍之官，悉著縗斬，唯著鎧不異，此即可擬。

translations.literal: Though today there is no office of attendants for the late emperor’s spirit seat, according to when Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died, at the completion of mourning dress the attendant officers all wore the coarsest hemp, differing only in that they still wore armor—this may serve as a model.
translations.idiomatic: There is no formal office of spirit-seat attendants now, but when Liang’s Crown Prince Zhaoming died his attendants at the completion of mourning all wore the coarsest hemp, except that they still wore armor. That is our model.

sentences.zh: 愚謂六日成服，俠靈座須服縗絰。

translations.literal: I hold that on the sixth day, when mourning dress is completed, those attending the spirit seat must wear hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day, when mourning dress is completed, attendants at the spirit seat should wear hemp mourning.

sentences.zh: 」中書舍人蔡景歷亦云：「雖不悉準，按山陵有凶吉羽儀，成服唯凶無吉，文武俠御，不容獨鳴玉珥貂，情禮二三，理宜縗斬。

translations.literal: " Palace Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Jingli also said: "Though it does not fully accord, according to the fact that for the imperial tomb there are auspicious and inauspicious regalia, and completion of mourning dress has only the inauspicious and not the auspicious, civil and military attendants cannot alone wear jade pendants and sable tails; in feeling and ritual there are two or three points, and they ought to wear coarse hemp.
translations.idiomatic: " Cai Jingli, palace secretariat attendant-in-ordinary, also said: "The tomb procession has both auspicious and mourning regalia, but completion of mourning dress is mourning only. Civil and military attendants cannot alone wear jade and sable. In ritual feeling they should wear coarse hemp."

sentences.zh: 」中書舍人江德藻、謝岐等並同師知議。

translations.literal: " Palace Secretariat Attendants Jiang Dezao, Xie Qi, and others all agreed with Shizhi’s view.
translations.idiomatic: Palace secretariat attendants Jiang Dezao, Xie Qi, and others all sided with Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 文阿重議云：「檢晉、宋山陵儀：『靈輿梓宮降殿，各侍中奏。

translations.literal: Wen’a argued again: "Checking the Jin and Song tomb protocols: ‘When the spirit carriage and inner coffin descend to the hall, each attendant-in-ordinary reports.’
translations.idiomatic: Wen’a replied: "The Jin and Song tomb protocols say: ‘When the spirit carriage and inner coffin descend to the hall, each attendant-in-ordinary reports.’

sentences.zh: 』又成服儀稱：『靈輿梓宮容俠御官及香橙。

translations.literal: The protocol for completing mourning dress also says: ‘The spirit carriage and inner coffin accommodate attendant officers and incense and oranges.’
translations.idiomatic: The protocol for completing mourning dress also says: ‘The spirit carriage and inner coffin accommodate attendant officers, incense, and oranges.’

sentences.zh: 』又檢靈輿梓宮進止儀稱：『直靈俠御吉服，在吉鹵簿中。

translations.literal: Checking again the protocol for the spirit carriage and inner coffin’s advance and halt, it says: ‘Direct attendants at the spirit seat wear auspicious dress and are in the auspicious guard of honor.’
translations.idiomatic: The protocol for the spirit carriage’s advance and halt says: ‘Direct attendants at the spirit seat wear auspicious dress and stand in the auspicious guard of honor.’

sentences.zh: 』又云：『梓宮俠御縗服，在凶鹵簿中。

translations.literal: It also says: ‘Attendants at the inner coffin wear hemp mourning and are in the inauspicious guard of honor.’
translations.idiomatic: It also says: ‘Attendants at the inner coffin wear hemp mourning and stand in the inauspicious guard of honor.’

sentences.zh: 』是則在殿吉凶兩俠御也。

translations.literal: Thus in the hall there are both auspicious and inauspicious attendants.
translations.idiomatic: So in the hall there are both auspicious and mourning attendants."

sentences.zh: 」時以二議不同，乃啟取左丞徐陵決斷。

translations.literal: At the time, because the two arguments differed, they submitted a memorial asking Left Vice Director Xu Ling to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Because the two sides disagreed, they asked left vice director Xu Ling to decide.

sentences.zh: 陵云：「梓宮祔山陵，靈筵祔宗廟，有此分判，便驗吉凶。

translations.literal: Ling said: "The inner coffin is lodged at the mountain tomb and the spirit couch at the ancestral temple—there is this division, and from it auspicious and inauspicious are verified.
translations.idiomatic: Ling said: "The inner coffin goes to the tomb and the spirit couch to the ancestral temple. That division itself shows what is auspicious and what is mourning.

sentences.zh: 按山陵鹵簿吉部

translations.literal: According to the auspicious section of the tomb guard of honor
translations.idiomatic: In the auspicious section of the tomb guard of honor

translations.literal: (office)
translations.idiomatic: (office)

sentences.zh: 〔伍〕中，[8]公卿以下導引者，爰及武賁、鼓吹、執蓋、奉車，[9]並是吉服，豈容俠御獨為縗絰邪？

translations.literal: [8] in the [five] ranks, from the dukes and ministers down through those who lead the procession, as well as the tiger guards, musicians, canopy bearers, and chariot attendants—all wear auspicious dress. How could the spirit-seat attendants alone wear hemp mourning?
translations.idiomatic: [8] in the fifth rank, from dukes and ministers down through guides, tiger guards, musicians, canopy bearers, and chariot attendants—all wear auspicious dress. How could spirit-seat attendants alone wear hemp mourning?

sentences.zh: 斷可知矣。

translations.literal: The conclusion is clear.
translations.idiomatic: The answer is plain.

sentences.zh: 若言公卿胥吏並服縗苴，此與梓宮部伍有何差別？

translations.literal: If one says that dukes, ministers, clerks, and attendants all wear hemp cloth, what difference is there between them and the inner-coffin guard?
translations.idiomatic: If dukes, ministers, clerks, and attendants all wore hemp, how would they differ from the inner-coffin guard?

sentences.zh: 若言文物並吉，司事者凶，豈容

translations.literal: If one says that ritual objects are all auspicious but those who manage affairs are inauspicious, how could one
translations.idiomatic: If ritual objects are auspicious but those who manage affairs are in mourning, how could one

sentences.zh: 〔衽〕絰而奉華蓋，[10]縗衣而升玉輅邪？

translations.literal: [10] [lapels] wear hemp at the lapels yet hold the state canopy, or wear mourning robes yet mount the jade chariot?
translations.idiomatic: [10] wear hemp at the lapels yet hold the state canopy, or wear mourning robes yet mount the jade chariot?

sentences.zh: 同博士議。

translations.literal: I agree with the academician’s view.
translations.idiomatic: I agree with the academician."

sentences.zh: 」師知又議曰：「左丞引梓宮祔山陵，靈筵祔宗廟，必有吉凶二部，成服不容上凶，博士猶執前斷，終是山陵之禮。

translations.literal: Shizhi argued again: "The left vice director cites the inner coffin lodged at the mountain tomb and the spirit couch at the ancestral temple, saying there must be auspicious and inauspicious sections; completion of mourning dress cannot have the upper part inauspicious. The academician still holds to his former decision, which is ultimately the tomb protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi argued again: "The left vice director says the inner coffin goes to the tomb and the spirit couch to the temple, so there must be auspicious and mourning sections, and completion of mourning dress cannot have mourning above. The academician still holds to the tomb rite.

sentences.zh: 若龍駕啟殯，鑾輿兼設，吉凶之儀，由來本備，準之成服，愚有未安。

translations.literal: If when the imperial carriage begins the funeral procession both regalia are set out together, auspicious and inauspicious protocols have from the outset been complete—measured against completion of mourning dress, I am still uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage begins the funeral both regalia are already in place. Measured against completion of mourning dress, I am still uneasy.

sentences.zh: 夫喪禮之制，自天子達。

translations.literal: The regulations of mourning rites extend from the Son of Heaven down.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning regulations extend from the Son of Heaven downward.

sentences.zh: 按王文憲喪服明記云：『官品第三，侍靈人二十。

translations.literal: According to Wang Wenhien’s Explanations of Mourning Dress it states: ‘For officials of the third rank, twenty persons attend the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenhien’s Explanations of Mourning Dress says: ‘For officials of the third rank, twenty persons attend the spirit.

sentences.zh: 官品第四，下達士禮，侍靈之數，並有十人。

translations.literal: For the fourth rank down to the scholar’s rites, the number attending the spirit is ten in each case.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth rank down to the scholar’s rite, ten attend the spirit in each case.

sentences.zh: 皆白布袴褶，著白絹帽。

translations.literal: All wear white-cloth trousers and jackets and white-silk caps.
translations.idiomatic: All wear white-cloth trousers and jackets and white-silk caps.

sentences.zh: 內喪女侍數如外，而著齊縗。

translations.literal: For inner mourning, female attendants are as numerous as the outer, but they wear the second-grade hemp.
translations.idiomatic: For inner mourning the women attendants match the men in number but wear second-grade hemp.

sentences.zh: 或問內外侍靈是同，何忽縗服有異？

translations.literal: Someone asked: if inner and outer attendants to the spirit are the same, why suddenly is mourning dress different?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: if inner and outer attendants are the same, why is mourning dress different?

sentences.zh: 答云，若依君臣之禮，則外侍斬，內侍齊。

translations.literal: The answer was: if one follows the rites of ruler and minister, then the outer attendants wear the coarsest cut and the inner the second grade.
translations.idiomatic: The answer was: by ruler-and-minister rites the outer attendants wear the coarsest cut and the inner the second grade.

sentences.zh: 頃世多故，禮隨事省。

translations.literal: In recent generations there have been many troubles, and rites have been reduced as affairs required.
translations.idiomatic: Recent ages have seen many troubles, and rites were cut to fit the times.

sentences.zh: 諸侯以下，臣吏蓋微，至於侍奉，多出義附，君臣之節不全，縗冠之費實闕，所以因其常服，止變帽而已。

translations.literal: Below the rank of feudal lord, ministers and clerks were slight; as for attendance, most came from voluntary attachment. The relation of ruler and minister was not complete, and the expense of hemp caps was in fact lacking; therefore they kept their ordinary dress and only changed the cap.
translations.idiomatic: Below feudal lords, officials were humble and attendants mostly volunteers. Ruler-minister form was incomplete and hemp caps too costly, so they kept ordinary dress and only changed the cap.

sentences.zh: 婦人侍者，皆是卑隸，君妾之道既純，服章所以備矣。

translations.literal: Women who attended were all low servants; the way of lord and concubine was pure, and therefore their dress and insignia were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Women attendants were low servants; lord and concubine stood apart, so their dress was complete.’

sentences.zh: 』皇朝之典，猶自不然，以此而推，是知服斬。

translations.literal: The statutes of our dynasty are still not so; from this one infers that the coarsest hemp should be worn.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty’s code is not like that. From this one infers coarse hemp.

sentences.zh: 彼有侍靈，則猶俠御，既著白帽，理無彤服。

translations.literal: Where there are attendants to the spirit, it is like attendants at the seat; once they wear the white cap, by principle there can be no colored dress.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit attendants are like seat attendants; in white caps they cannot wear colored dress.

sentences.zh: 且梁昭明儀注，今則見存，二文顯證，差為成準。

translations.literal: Moreover the Liang protocols for Crown Prince Zhaoming still exist today; these two texts are clear evidence and may serve as a settled standard.
translations.idiomatic: Liang’s protocols for Crown Prince Zhaoming still survive. Those two texts are clear proof and a settled standard.

sentences.zh: 且禮出人情，可得消息。

translations.literal: Moreover rites arise from human feeling and may be adjusted in message.
translations.idiomatic: Rites arise from feeling and may be adjusted in practice.

sentences.zh: 凡人有喪，既陳筵机，繐帷靈屏，[11]變其常儀，蘆箔草廬，即其凶禮。

translations.literal: Whenever anyone has a bereavement, once the spirit couch and offering tables are set out, curtains and spirit screens are hung, [11] ordinary observances are changed, and reed mats and grass huts are the inauspicious rite.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone mourns, once the spirit couch and tables are set out and curtains hung, ordinary life changes; reed mats and grass huts are the mourning rite.

sentences.zh: 堂室之內，親賓具來，齊斬麻緦，差池哭次，玄冠不弔，莫非素服。

translations.literal: Within the hall, kin and guests all come; in coarse hemp of various grades they take their places weeping in ranks; black caps do not pay condolence calls—all are plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Within the hall kin and guests gather in hemp of every grade, weeping in ranks. Black caps do not call—all wear plain dress.

sentences.zh: 豈見門生故吏，綃縠間趨，左姬右姜，紅紫相糅？

translations.literal: How could one see students and old retainers hurrying in silk and gauze, with concubines left and right in red and purple mingled?
translations.idiomatic: Who could see students and retainers rushing about in silk, with concubines in red and purple at their sides?

sentences.zh: 況四海遏密，率土之情是同，三軍縞素，為服之制斯壹。

translations.literal: How much more when the realm is in deep mourning and feeling under Heaven is one; the three armies in plain white—the regulation of dress is uniform.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the realm is in deep mourning and all under Heaven feels as one, and the three armies wear plain white in a single regulation of dress.

sentences.zh: 遂使千門旦啟，非塗堊於彤闈，百僚戾止，變服麤於朱韍，而耀金在列，鳴玉節行，求之懷抱，固為未愜，準以禮經，彌無前事。

translations.literal: Thus a thousand gates open at dawn—not whitewash on the vermilion gate; the hundred officials arrive and stop—coarse dress replaces the vermilion sash; yet gleaming gold stands in the ranks and sounding jade marks the procession. Sought in the heart, it is plainly unsatisfying; measured against the ritual canon, there is even less precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a thousand gates open at dawn without whitewash on the vermilion gate; the hundred officials arrive in coarse dress instead of vermilion sashes, while gold gleams in the ranks and jade sounds in procession. In the heart it cannot satisfy; by the ritual canon there is no precedent.

sentences.zh: 豈可成服之儀，譬以山陵之禮？

translations.literal: How can the rites of completing mourning dress be likened to the tomb protocol?
translations.idiomatic: How can completion of mourning dress be likened to the tomb rites?

sentences.zh: 葬既始終已畢，故有吉凶之儀，所謂成服，本成喪禮，百司外內，皆變吉容，俠御獨不，何謂成服？

translations.literal: When burial has begun and ended, there are therefore auspicious and inauspicious protocols—what is called completing mourning dress is fundamentally completing the mourning rite. Inside and outside, the hundred offices all change to auspicious appearance; if the spirit-seat attendants alone do not, what is called completing mourning dress?
translations.idiomatic: When burial is finished there are auspicious and mourning protocols. Completing mourning dress means completing the mourning rite. All offices inside and out change to auspicious dress—if spirit-seat attendants alone do not, what is completion of mourning?

sentences.zh: 若靈無俠御則已，有則必應縗服。

translations.literal: If there are no spirit-seat attendants, so be it; if there are, they must wear hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: If there are no spirit-seat attendants, so be it; if there are, they must wear hemp mourning."

sentences.zh: 」謝岐議曰：「靈筵祔宗廟，梓宮祔山陵，實如左丞議。

translations.literal: Xie Qi argued: "The spirit couch is lodged at the ancestral temple and the inner coffin at the mountain tomb—this is truly as the left vice director said.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qi argued: "The spirit couch goes to the temple and the inner coffin to the tomb, as the left vice director said.

sentences.zh: 但山陵鹵簿，備有吉凶，從靈輿者儀服無變，從梓宮者皆服苴縗。

translations.literal: But in the tomb guard of honor auspicious and inauspicious are both provided; those who follow the spirit carriage do not change dress, while those who follow the inner coffin all wear hemp cloth.
translations.idiomatic: But the tomb guard has both auspicious and mourning sections. Those who follow the spirit carriage keep their dress; those who follow the inner coffin all wear hemp.

sentences.zh: 爰至士禮，悉同此制，此自是山陵之儀，非關成服。

translations.literal: Down to the scholar’s rites all follow this regulation—this is itself the tomb protocol and does not concern completion of mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the scholar’s rite the rule is the same. That is the tomb rite, not completion of mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 今謂梓宮靈扆，共在西階，稱為成服，亦無鹵簿，直是爰自胥吏，上至王公，四海之內，必備縗絰。

translations.literal: Now we call the inner coffin and spirit screen both on the western steps ‘completing mourning dress,’ yet there is no guard of honor—only from clerks and attendants up to dukes and ministers, within the four seas, all must wear hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Now the inner coffin and spirit screen both stand on the western steps and we call it completing mourning dress, yet there is no guard of honor—only that from clerks to dukes, throughout the realm, all must wear hemp.

sentences.zh: 案梁昭明太子薨，略是成例，豈容凡百士庶，悉皆服重，而侍中至於武衛，最是近官，反鳴玉紆青，與平吉不異？

translations.literal: According to when Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died, which is roughly the established example—how could common scholars and people all wear the heavy grade, while attendants-in-ordinary down to the martial guards, who are the nearest officers, on the contrary sound jade and twist azure, no different from ordinary auspicious days?
translations.idiomatic: When Liang’s Crown Prince Zhaoming died is the established example. How could every commoner wear the heavy grade while attendants-in-ordinary down to the martial guards—the nearest officers—wore jade and azure no differently from an ordinary auspicious day?

sentences.zh: 左丞既推以山陵事，愚意或謂與成服有殊。

translations.literal: The left vice director, pushing the matter of the tomb, in my humble view perhaps differs from completion of mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: The left vice director treats it as a tomb matter; I think that may differ from completion of mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 若爾日俠御，文武不異，維侍靈之人，主書、宣傳、齊幹、應敕，悉應不改。

translations.literal: If on that day the spirit-seat attendants, civil and military, were not different, then those who attend the spirit—the chief clerks, heralds, runners, and responders to edicts—should all likewise not change.
translations.idiomatic: If on that day spirit-seat attendants, civil and military alike, were unchanged, then chief clerks, heralds, runners, and responders to edicts who attend the spirit should likewise not change."

sentences.zh: 」蔡景歷又議云：「俠御之官，本出五百，爾日備服居廬，仍於本省，引上登殿，豈應變服貂玉？

translations.literal: Cai Jingli argued again: "The office of spirit-seat attendants originally came from the five hundred; on that day, though they wore mourning dress and dwelt in the mourning hut, they were still in their original department and were led up to ascend the hall—how could they change to sable and jade?
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jingli argued again: "Spirit-seat attendants came from the five hundred. That day they wore mourning dress and dwelt in the mourning hut but still belonged to their offices and were led up to the hall—how could they change to sable and jade?

sentences.zh: 若別攝餘官，以充簪珥，則爾日便有不成服者。

translations.literal: If other officials were specially assigned to fill the ranks of insignia, then on that day there would be some who had not completed mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: If other officers were drafted to fill the insignia ranks, then on that day some would not have completed mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 山陵自有吉凶二議，成服凶而不吉，猶依前議，同劉舍人。

translations.literal: The tomb has its own debate on auspicious and inauspicious; completion of mourning dress is inauspicious and not auspicious—still following the former view, I agree with Attendant Liu.
translations.idiomatic: The tomb has its own auspicious-and-mourning debate. Completion of mourning dress is mourning, not auspicious. I still follow the former view and agree with Attendant Liu."

sentences.zh: 」德藻又議云：「愚謂祖葬之辰，始終永畢，達官有追贈，須表恩榮，有吉鹵簿，恐由此義，私家放效，因以成俗。

translations.literal: Dezao argued again: "I hold that on the day of the ancestral burial, when beginning and end are forever complete, high officials receive posthumous honors and must display grace and glory; there is an auspicious guard of honor, and I fear the meaning lies here. Private families imitated it, and thus it became custom.
translations.idiomatic: Dezao argued again: "On the day of ancestral burial, when the rite is forever complete, high officials receive posthumous honors and display grace. The auspicious guard may come from that. Private families imitated it and it became custom.

sentences.zh: 上服本變吉為凶，理不應猶襲紈綺。

translations.literal: Upper dress fundamentally changes from auspicious to inauspicious; by principle one should not still wear silk gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Upper dress should change from auspicious to mourning; by principle one should not still wear silk gauze.

sentences.zh: 劉舍人引王衛軍喪儀及檢梁昭明故事，此明據已審，博士、左丞乃各盡事衷，既未取證，須更詢詳，宜諮八座、詹事、太常、中丞

translations.literal: Attendant Liu cited General Wang’s mourning protocol and checked the Liang Zhaoming precedent—this clear evidence is already established. The academician and left vice director each exhausted their views; since no proof was taken, inquiry must go further. It should be put to the eight ministers, the household tutor of the heir apparent, the minister of rites, the censor-in-chief
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Liu cited General Wang’s mourning protocol and the Liang Zhaoming precedent—clear proof already in hand. The academician and left vice director each stated his view; since no decision was reached, inquiry should go further—to the eight ministers, the heir apparent’s tutor, the minister of rites, the censor-in-chief

translations.idiomatic: (Kong)

sentences.zh: 〔及〕中庶諸通袁樞、張種、周弘正、弘讓、沈炯、孔奐[12]。

translations.literal: [12] and the household tutors and general attendants Yuan Shu, Zhang Zhong, Zhou Hongzheng, Hongrang, Shen Jiong, and Kong Huan.
translations.idiomatic: [12] and the household tutors and general attendants Yuan Shu, Zhang Zhong, Zhou Hongzheng, Hongrang, Shen Jiong, and Kong Huan."

sentences.zh: 」時八座以下，並請：「案群議，斟酌舊儀，梁昭明太子喪成服儀注，明文見存，足為準的。

translations.literal: At that time the eight ministers and below all requested: "Considering the group discussions and weighing old protocol, the Liang protocols for completing mourning dress at Crown Prince Zhaoming’s death exist in clear text today and suffice as a standard.
translations.idiomatic: The eight ministers and below all submitted: "Weighing the discussions and old protocol, Liang’s protocols for completing mourning dress at Crown Prince Zhaoming’s death survive in clear text and suffice as standard.

sentences.zh: 成服日，侍官理不容猶從吉禮。

translations.literal: On the day of completing mourning dress, attendant officers by principle cannot still follow auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of completing mourning dress, attendant officers cannot follow auspicious rites.

sentences.zh: 其葬禮分吉，自是山陵之時，非關成服之日。

translations.literal: That burial rites are divided into auspicious sections is a matter of the time of the mountain tomb and does not concern the day of completing mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Burial rites divide into auspicious sections at the tomb; that does not concern the day of completing mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 愚謂劉舍人議於事為允。

translations.literal: I hold that Attendant Liu’s view is acceptable in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that Attendant Liu’s view is acceptable."

sentences.zh: 」陵重答云：「老病屬纊，不能多說，古人爭議，多成怨府，傅玄見尤於晉代，王商取陷於漢朝，謹自三緘，敬同高命。

translations.literal: Ling answered again: "Old and ill, I lie with the coverlet up to my chin and cannot say much. Men of old who disputed often became objects of resentment; Fu Xuan was blamed in the Jin age and Wang Shang fell into trouble in Han—I respectfully seal my lips thrice and honor your high command.
translations.idiomatic: Ling answered again: "Old and ill, I can say little. Men of old who disputed often bred resentment; Fu Xuan was blamed in Jin and Wang Shang fell in Han. I seal my lips thrice and honor your command.

sentences.zh: 若萬一不死，猶得展言，庶與朝賢更申揚搉。

translations.literal: If by any chance I do not die, I may yet speak further and, with the court worthies, discuss again in detail.
translations.idiomatic: If by chance I do not die, I may yet speak and discuss the matter again with the court."

sentences.zh: 」文阿猶執所見，眾議不能決，乃具錄二議奏聞，從師知議。

translations.literal: Wen’a still held to his view; the assembly could not decide, so they fully recorded both arguments and submitted them, following Shizhi’s view.
translations.idiomatic: Wen’a still held to his view. The assembly could not decide, recorded both arguments, submitted them, and followed Shizhi’s view.

sentences.zh: 尋遷鴻臚卿，舍人如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister Herald, his post as Attendant-in-Ordinary unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made minister herald, keeping his post as attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year one he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖敕師知撰起居注，自永定二年秋至天嘉元年冬，為十卷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen had ordered Shizhi to compile the imperial diary from the autumn of Yongding year two to the winter of Tianjia year one, ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Wen had ordered Shizhi to compile the imperial diary from autumn of Yongding year two through winter of Tianjia year one—ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 起為中書舍人，復掌詔誥。

translations.literal: He was raised as Palace Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary and again put in charge of edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as palace secretariat attendant-in-ordinary and again put in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，世祖不豫，師知與尚書僕射到仲舉等入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang, when Emperor Wen was ill, Shizhi together with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Dao Zhongju and others entered to attend with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiankang year one, when Emperor Wen fell ill, Shizhi with vice director of the masters of writing Dao Zhongju and others entered to tend him with medicine.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，預受顧命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, he received the testamentary charge in advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, Shizhi had already received the deathbed charge.

sentences.zh: 及高宗為尚書令，入輔，光大元年，師知與仲舉等遣舍人殷不佞矯詔令高宗還東府，事覺，於北獄賜死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was Director of the Masters of Writing and entered to assist, in the first year of Guangda, Shizhi together with Zhongju and others sent Attendant Yin Buniu with a forged order telling Emperor Xuan to return to the Eastern Mansion; the affair was discovered and at the northern prison he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was director of the masters of writing and regent, in Guangda year one Shizhi with Zhongju and others sent attendant Yin Buniu with a forged order telling Emperor Xuan to return to the Eastern Mansion. The plot was exposed and he was granted death in the northern prison.

sentences.zh: 謝岐，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Xie Qi was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qi was from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父達，梁太學博士。

translations.literal: His father Da was a Liang Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Da was a Liang erudite of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 岐少機警，好學，見稱於梁世。

translations.literal: Qi in youth was quick-witted, loved learning, and was praised in the Liang age.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was quick-witted as a youth, loved learning, and won praise under Liang.

sentences.zh: 為尚書金部郎，山陰令。

translations.literal: He was Lang of the Ministry of Revenue in the Masters of Writing and Magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was a revenue clerk in the masters of writing and magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，岐流寓東陽。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Qi wandered in Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Qi took refuge in Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 景平，依于張彪。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, he attached himself to Zhang Biao.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing was suppressed he joined Zhang Biao.

sentences.zh: 彪在吳郡及會稽，庶事一以委之。

translations.literal: When Biao was in Wu commandery and Kuaiji, he entrusted all miscellaneous affairs to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao held Wu and Kuaiji he entrusted all routine affairs to Qi.

sentences.zh: 彪每征討，恆留岐監郡，知後事。

translations.literal: Whenever Biao went on campaign, he always left Qi to supervise the commandery and manage subsequent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Biao campaigned he left Qi to supervise the commandery and handle affairs behind him.

sentences.zh: 彪敗，高祖引岐參預機密，以為兼尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When Biao was defeated, the Founder drew Qi into confidential planning and made him Acting Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao was defeated the Founder drew Qi into confidential planning and made him acting right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅屢興，糧儲多闕，岐所在幹理，深被知遇。

translations.literal: At that time campaigns were frequent and grain stores often lacked; wherever Qi took charge of affairs he was deeply known and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns were frequent and grain stores often empty; wherever Qi managed affairs he won deep trust.

sentences.zh: 永定元年，為給事黃門侍郎、中書舍人，兼右丞如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongding he was made Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Palace Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary, still acting right vice director as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year one he was made attendant of the yellow gate and palace secretariat attendant-in-ordinary, still acting right vice director.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年卒，贈通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjia he died; he was posthumously made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year two he died and was posthumously made regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 岐弟嶠，篤學，為世通儒。

translations.literal: Qi’s younger brother Qiao was devoted to learning and was a Confucian master of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Qi’s younger brother Qiao was devoted to learning and a leading Confucian of the age.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：高祖開基創業，剋定禍亂，武猛固其立功，文翰亦乃展力。

translations.literal: The historian says: When the Founder opened the foundation and created the enterprise, quelling disaster and disorder, martial fierceness indeed established his achievement, but literary writing also displayed its power.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: When the Founder raised the dynasty and quelled chaos, martial prowess won his achievement, but literary men also played their part.

sentences.zh: [13]趙知禮、蔡景歷早識攀附，預締構之臣焉。

translations.literal: [13] Zhao Zhili and Cai Jingli early recognized and attached themselves to him; they were ministers in the founding structure.
translations.idiomatic: [13] Zhao Zhili and Cai Jingli recognized him early and helped build the state.

sentences.zh: 劉師知博涉多通，而闇於機變，雖欲存乎節義，終陷極刑，斯不智矣。

translations.literal: Liu Shizhi ranged widely and knew much, yet was dark about timely change; though he wished to preserve integrity and righteousness, in the end he fell to extreme punishment—this was lack of wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shizhi was broadly learned but blind to the moment; though he wished to keep his integrity, he ended on the execution ground—this was folly.

translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Liu Shizhi〉

translations.idiomatic: "Kong Central Palace Attendant Zhu Tong"—doubtful.

sentences.zh: 莫不預〔焉〕據北監本、汲本、殿本及《南史》補。

translations.literal: None of the plans was not participated in [by him]—[yan] supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: On "none of the plans was not participated in": yan supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 子允恭嗣 殿本考證云「允」《南史》作「元」。

translations.literal: His son Yun'gong succeeded—Hall edition verification says the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Yuan for Yun.
translations.idiomatic: On "his son Yun'gong succeeded": the Hall edition notes the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Yuan for Yun.

sentences.zh: 衡陽獻王〔昌〕時為吳興郡昌年尚少 據《元龜》七〇八、七二七補。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang [Chang], when he was Administrator of Wuxing—Chang was still young—[Chang] supplied according to Yuan Gui 708 and 727.
translations.idiomatic: On "Prince Xian of Hengyang when Administrator of Wuxing, Chang still young": Chang supplied per Yuan Gui 708 and 727.

sentences.zh: 錢大昕《廿二史考異》云當移「昌」字於「衡陽獻王」之下。

translations.literal: Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies among the Twenty-two Histories says the character Chang should be moved to below Prince Xian of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daxin holds the character Chang should stand under Prince Xian of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 今按：此特「衡陽獻王」下脫一「昌」字耳，下「昌」字不當移。

translations.literal: Present review: only a missing Chang under Prince Xian of Hengyang; the Chang below should not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Present review: only one Chang is missing after Prince Xian of Hengyang; the lower Chang should not be moved.

sentences.zh: 并受歐陽武威餉絹百匹 殿本考證雲南史無「武」字。

translations.literal: Also received one hundred bolts of silk as gift from Ouyang Wuwei—Hall edition verification says the History of the Southern Dynasties lacks the character Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On "also received one hundred bolts of silk from Ouyang Wuwei": the Hall edition notes the History of the Southern Dynasties omits Wu.

sentences.zh: 今按：此亦改復名為單名，《南史》往往如此。

translations.literal: Present review: this too changes a restored full name to a single name; the History of the Southern Dynasties often does so.
translations.idiomatic: Present review: here too a full name is reduced to a single character, as the History of the Southern Dynasties often does.

sentences.zh: 兼太舟卿 「太舟卿」南監本、汲本、殿本並作「太府卿」。

translations.literal: Concurrently Grand Boat Minister—"Grand Boat Minister" in the Southern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions all read Grand Storehouse Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On "concurrently Grand Boat Minister": the Southern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions all read Grand Storehouse Minister.

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「『府』監本誤『舟』，今改正。

translations.literal: Hall edition verification says: "'fu' in the Supervisory edition was wrongly written 'zhou'; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall edition holds the Supervisory edition wrongly wrote zhou for fu and emended it—note:

sentences.zh: 」今按：梁天監七年，以都水使者為太舟卿，為列卿之最末者，主舟航堤渠，見《隋書·百官志》，殿本妄改。

translations.literal: " Present review: In the seventh year of Liang Tianjian, the Commissioner of Waterways was made Grand Boat Minister, lowest among the regular ministers, overseeing boats and embankments—see the Treatise on Officials in the Book of Sui; the Hall edition wrongly emended.
translations.idiomatic: Present review: in Liang Tianjian year 7 the commissioner of waterways became Grand Boat Minister, the lowest regular minister, in charge of shipping and dikes (Book of Sui, Treatise on Officials); the Hall emendation is wrong.

sentences.zh: 宣毅長沙王長史 「宣毅」汲本作「宣豫」，殿本依北監本作「宣義」。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator to the Prince of Changsha, Xuan-yi [style]—"Xuan-yi" in the Ji edition reads "Xuan-yu"; the Hall edition, following the Northern Supervisory, reads "Xuan-yi" (yi as righteousness).
translations.idiomatic: On "chief administrator to the Xuan-yi Prince of Changsha": Ji reads Xuan-yu; Hall follows the Northern Supervisory with Xuan-yi (alternate graph).

sentences.zh: 按長沙王陳叔堅於太建四年為宣毅將軍，作「宣毅」是。

translations.literal: Comment: Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian was made General of Resolute Declaration in the fourth year of Taijian; to write "Resolute Declaration" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian became general of resolute declaration in Taijian year 4, so the title xuan-yi (resolute declaration) is correct.

sentences.zh: 帝令有司按問 「帝」原訛「章」，今據北監本、汲本、殿本及《南史》、《元龜》五一九改正。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the responsible offices to investigate—"Emperor" was originally corrupted as "Zhang"; now corrected according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions, the History of the Southern Dynasties, and Yuan Gui 519.
translations.idiomatic: On "the Emperor ordered inquiry": Di was written Zhang; emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions, the History of the Southern Dynasties, and Yuan Gui 519.

translations.idiomatic: On "[Wu] within": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Hall editions, and History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 爰及武賁鼓吹執蓋奉車 「武賁」即「虎賁」，避唐諱改。

translations.idiomatic: On "and extending to martial tiger guard, drum-and-pipe, canopy-bearers, and chariot attendants": wu-ben renders hu-ben, taboo-changed for Tang.

translations.idiomatic: On "[ren] with mourning sash yet bearing the imperial canopy": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Hall editions, and History of the Southern Dynasties.

translations.idiomatic: On "curtained bier, spirit screen": the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read chamber for screen.

translations.literal: Says: "'chamber' is a mistake for 'yi-back'; screen and yi-back are one thing.
translations.idiomatic: writes: "Chamber is an error for yi; screen and yi are the same object.

translations.idiomatic: On "literary brush also then deployed its strength": the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read gan (administer) for han (brush).
